Action.leftRegularTensorIso.comment:
Given `X : Action (Type u) (Mon.of G)` for `G` a group, then `G × X` (with `G` acting as left
multiplication on the first factor and by `X.ρ` on the second) is isomorphic as a `G`-set to
`G × X` (with `G` acting as left multiplication on the first factor and trivially on the second).

Action.leftRegularTensorIso.fullDefinition: noncomputable def leftRegularTensorIso (G : Type u) [Group G] (X : Action (Type u) (MonCat.of G)) :     leftRegular G ⊗ X ≅ leftRegular G ⊗ Action.mk X.V 1 where   hom :=     { hom := fun g => ⟨g.1, (X.ρ (g.1⁻¹ : G) g.2 : X.V)⟩       comm := fun (g : G) => by         funext ⟨(x₁ : G), (x₂ : X.V)⟩         refine Prod.ext rfl ?_         change (X.ρ ((g * x₁)⁻¹ : G) * X.ρ g) x₂ = X.ρ _ _         rw [mul_inv_rev, ← X.ρ.map_mul, inv_mul_cancel_right] }   inv :=     { hom := fun g => ⟨g.1, X.ρ g.1 g.2⟩       comm := fun (g : G) => by         funext ⟨(x₁ : G), (x₂ : X.V)⟩         refine Prod.ext rfl ?_         erw [tensor_rho, tensor_rho]         dsimp         -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644         erw [leftRegular_ρ_apply]         erw [map_mul]         rfl }   hom_inv_id := by     apply Hom.ext     funext x     refine Prod.ext rfl ?_     change (X.ρ x.1 * X.ρ (x.1⁻¹ : G)) x.2 = x.2     rw [← X.ρ.map_mul, mul_inv_self, X.ρ.map_one, MonCat.one_of, End.one_def, types_id_apply]   inv_hom_id := by     apply Hom.ext     funext x     refine Prod.ext rfl ?_     change (X.ρ (x.1⁻¹ : G) * X.ρ x.1) x.2 = x.2     rw [← X.ρ.map_mul, inv_mul_self, X.ρ.map_one, MonCat.one_of, End.one_def, types_id_apply] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Representation.ofModule'.code:
Representation.ofModule'.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {k : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} [CommSemiring k] [Monoid G] (M : Type u_4)
  [AddCommMonoid M] [Module k M] [Module (MonoidAlgebra k G) M] [IsScalarTower k (MonoidAlgebra k G) M] :
  Representation k G M
Representation.ofModule'.comment:
Build a `Representation k G M` from a `[Module (MonoidAlgebra k G) M]`.

This version is not always what we want, as it relies on an existing `[Module k M]`
instance, along with a `[IsScalarTower k (MonoidAlgebra k G) M]` instance.

We remedy this below in `ofModule`
(with the tradeoff that the representation is defined
only on a type synonym of the original module.)

explanatories.MonoidAlgebra.lift: This definition establishes a correspondence between commutative monoid homomorphisms and algebra homomorphisms from a monoid algebra to another algebra over the same semiring.
explanatories.AddEquiv.symm: The definition states that the inverse of an additive isomorphism is also an additive isomorphism.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Algebra.lsmul: This definition describes an algebra morphism that represents the action of one algebra on a module, which maps elements of that algebra to endomorphisms of the module while preserving the underlying scalar structure.
explanatories.RestrictScalars.lsmul: This definition describes an algebra homomorphism that maps elements from a semiring into endomorphisms of a module defined by restricting scalars from one algebra to another.

Representation.ofModule'.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofModule' (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module k M]     [Module (MonoidAlgebra k G) M] [IsScalarTower k (MonoidAlgebra k G) M] : Representation k G M :=   (MonoidAlgebra.lift k G (M →ₗ[k] M)).symm (Algebra.lsmul k k M)
Representation.ofModule'.description: A representation of a monoid acting on a module is constructed from an existing module over the monoid algebra, accompanied by the conditions of a scalar tower, although this approach may not always be ideal.

  [CommSemiring k] [Group G] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module k V] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module k W] (ρV : Representation k G V)
  (ρW : Representation k G W) (g : G) :
  dualTensorHom k V W ∘ₗ TensorProduct.map (ρV.dual g) (ρW g) = (ρV.linHom ρW) g ∘ₗ dualTensorHom k V W
Representation.dualTensorHom_comm.comment:
Given $k$-modules $V, W$, there is a homomorphism $φ : V^* ⊗ W → Hom_k(V, W)$
(implemented by `LinearAlgebra.Contraction.dualTensorHom`).
Given representations of $G$ on $V$ and $W$,there are representations of $G$ on $V^* ⊗ W$ and on
$Hom_k(V, W)$.
This lemma says that $φ$ is $G$-linear.

Representation.dualTensorHom_comm.description: The composition of the dual tensor homomorphism with the map induced by group representations is equivalent to the application of the linear homomorphism between the representations followed by the dual tensor homomorphism, demonstrating that the dual tensor homomorphism respects the group structure.

Rep.leftRegularHomEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def leftRegularHomEquiv (A : Rep k G) : (Rep.ofMulAction k G G ⟶ A) ≃ₗ[k] A where   toFun f := f.hom (Finsupp.single 1 1)   map_add' x y := rfl   map_smul' r x := rfl   invFun x := leftRegularHom A x   left_inv f := by     refine Action.Hom.ext _ _ (Finsupp.lhom_ext' fun x : G => LinearMap.ext_ring ?_)     have :       f.hom ((ofMulAction k G G).ρ x (Finsupp.single (1 : G) (1 : k))) =         A.ρ x (f.hom (Finsupp.single (1 : G) (1 : k))) :=       LinearMap.ext_iff.1 (f.comm x) (Finsupp.single 1 1)     simp only [leftRegularHom_hom, LinearMap.comp_apply, Finsupp.lsingle_apply, Finsupp.lift_apply,       ← this, coe_of, of_ρ, Representation.ofMulAction_single x (1 : G) (1 : k), smul_eq_mul,       mul_one, zero_smul, Finsupp.sum_single_index, one_smul]     -- Mismatched `Zero k` instances     rfl   right_inv x := leftRegularHom_apply x set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Rep.left_regular_hom_equiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def leftRegularHomEquiv (A : Rep k G) : (Rep.ofMulAction k G G ⟶ A) ≃ₗ[k] A where   toFun f := f.hom (Finsupp.single 1 1)   map_add' x y := rfl   map_smul' r x := rfl   invFun x := leftRegularHom A x   left_inv f := by     refine Action.Hom.ext _ _ (Finsupp.lhom_ext' fun x : G => LinearMap.ext_ring ?_)     have :       f.hom ((ofMulAction k G G).ρ x (Finsupp.single (1 : G) (1 : k))) =         A.ρ x (f.hom (Finsupp.single (1 : G) (1 : k))) :=       LinearMap.ext_iff.1 (f.comm x) (Finsupp.single 1 1)     simp only [leftRegularHom_hom, LinearMap.comp_apply, Finsupp.lsingle_apply, Finsupp.lift_apply,       ← this, coe_of, of_ρ, Representation.ofMulAction_single x (1 : G) (1 : k), smul_eq_mul,       mul_one, zero_smul, Finsupp.sum_single_index, one_smul]     -- Mismatched `Zero k` instances     rfl   right_inv x := leftRegularHom_apply x set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

Rep.ihom.code: Rep.ihom.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) : Rep k G ⥤ Rep k G
Rep.ihom.comment:
Given a `k`-linear `G`-representation `(A, ρ₁)`, this is the 'internal Hom' functor sending
`(B, ρ₂)` to the representation `Homₖ(A, B)` that maps `g : G` and `f : A →ₗ[k] B` to
`(ρ₂ g) ∘ₗ f ∘ₗ (ρ₁ g⁻¹)`.

Rep.ihom.fullDefinition: protected def ihom (A : Rep k G) : Rep k G ⥤ Rep k G where   obj B := Rep.of (Representation.linHom A.ρ B.ρ)   map := fun {X} {Y} f =>     { hom := ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.llcomp k _ _ _ f.hom)       comm := fun g => LinearMap.ext fun x => LinearMap.ext fun y => by         show f.hom (X.ρ g _) = _         simp only [hom_comm_apply]; rfl }   map_id := fun _ => by ext; rfl   map_comp := fun _ _ => by ext; rfl set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Rep.ihom.description: This defines a functor that assigns to a given representation the space of homomorphisms from it to other representations, incorporating the action of a group on both the domain and codomain.

Rep.homEquiv.code: Rep.homEquiv.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A B C : Rep k G) : (A ⊗ B ⟶ C) ≃ (B ⟶ A.ihom.obj C)
Rep.homEquiv.comment:
Given a `k`-linear `G`-representation `A`, this is the Hom-set bijection in the adjunction
`A ⊗ - ⊣ ihom(A, -)`. It sends `f : A ⊗ B ⟶ C` to a `Rep k G` morphism defined by currying the
`k`-linear map underlying `f`, giving a map `A →ₗ[k] B →ₗ[k] C`, then flipping the arguments.

Rep.homEquiv.fullDefinition: def homEquiv (A B C : Rep k G) : (A ⊗ B ⟶ C) ≃ (B ⟶ (Rep.ihom A).obj C) where   toFun f :=     { hom := (TensorProduct.curry f.hom).flip       comm := fun g => by         refine LinearMap.ext fun x => LinearMap.ext fun y => ?_         change f.hom (_ ⊗ₜ[k] _) = C.ρ g (f.hom (_ ⊗ₜ[k] _))         rw [← hom_comm_apply]         change _ = f.hom ((A.ρ g * A.ρ g⁻¹) y ⊗ₜ[k] _)         simp only [← map_mul, mul_inv_self, map_one]         rfl }   invFun f :=     { hom := TensorProduct.uncurry k _ _ _ f.hom.flip       comm := fun g => TensorProduct.ext' fun x y => by /- Porting note: rest of broken proof was         dsimp only [MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft_obj, ModuleCat.comp_def, LinearMap.comp_apply,           tensor_rho, ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.hom_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul]         simp only [TensorProduct.uncurry_apply f.hom.flip, LinearMap.flip_apply, Action_ρ_eq_ρ,           hom_comm_apply f g y, Rep.ihom_obj_ρ_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, ρ_inv_self_apply] -/         change TensorProduct.uncurry k _ _ _ f.hom.flip (A.ρ g x ⊗ₜ[k] B.ρ g y) =           C.ρ g (TensorProduct.uncurry k _ _ _ f.hom.flip (x ⊗ₜ[k] y))         -- The next 3 tactics used to be `rw` before leanprover/lean4#2644         erw [TensorProduct.uncurry_apply, LinearMap.flip_apply, hom_comm_apply,           Rep.ihom_obj_ρ_apply,           LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply] --, ρ_inv_self_apply (A := C)]         dsimp         erw [ρ_inv_self_apply]         rfl}   left_inv f := Action.Hom.ext _ _ (TensorProduct.ext' fun _ _ => rfl)   right_inv f := by ext; rfl set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Rep.homEquiv.description: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence between the morphisms from the tensor product of two representations to a third representation and the morphisms from one representation to the internal hom of another representation, highlighting an adjunction relationship.

  diagonal G (n + 1) ≅ leftRegular G ⊗ { V := Fin n → G, ρ := 1 }
groupCohomology.resolution.actionDiagona.comment:
An isomorphism of `G`-sets `Gⁿ⁺¹ ≅ G × Gⁿ`, where `G` acts by left multiplication on `Gⁿ⁺¹` and
`G` but trivially on `Gⁿ`. The map sends `(g₀, ..., gₙ) ↦ (g₀, (g₀⁻¹g₁, g₁⁻¹g₂, ..., gₙ₋₁⁻¹gₙ))`,
and the inverse is `(g₀, (g₁, ..., gₙ)) ↦ (g₀, g₀g₁, g₀g₁g₂, ..., g₀g₁...gₙ).`

groupCohomology.resolution.diagonalSucc.comment:
An isomorphism of `k`-linear representations of `G` from `k[Gⁿ⁺¹]` to `k[G] ⊗ₖ k[Gⁿ]` (on
which `G` acts by `ρ(g₁)(g₂ ⊗ x) = (g₁ * g₂) ⊗ x`) sending `(g₀, ..., gₙ)` to
`g₀ ⊗ (g₀⁻¹g₁, g₁⁻¹g₂, ..., gₙ₋₁⁻¹gₙ)`. The inverse sends `g₀ ⊗ (g₁, ..., gₙ)` to
`(g₀, g₀g₁, ..., g₀g₁...gₙ)`.

groupCohomology.resolution.ofMulActionBa.comment:
The `k[G]`-linear isomorphism `k[G] ⊗ₖ k[Gⁿ] ≃ k[Gⁿ⁺¹]`, where the `k[G]`-module structure on
the lefthand side is `TensorProduct.leftModule`, whilst that of the righthand side comes from

groupCohomology.resolution.ofMulActionBa.fullDefinition: def ofMulActionBasisAux :     MonoidAlgebra k G ⊗[k] ((Fin n → G) →₀ k) ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra k G]       (ofMulAction k G (Fin (n + 1) → G)).asModule :=   { (Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra.1.mapIso (diagonalSucc k G n).symm).toLinearEquiv with     map_smul' := fun r x => by       -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644       erw [RingHom.id_apply, LinearEquiv.toFun_eq_coe, ← LinearEquiv.map_smul]       congr 1 /- Porting note (#11039): broken proof was       refine' x.induction_on _ (fun x y => _) fun y z hy hz => _       · simp only [smul_zero]       · simp only [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']         show (r * x) ⊗ₜ y = _         rw [← ofMulAction_self_smul_eq_mul, smul_tprod_one_asModule]       · rw [smul_add, hz, hy, smul_add] -/       show _ = Representation.asAlgebraHom (tensorObj (Rep.leftRegular k G)         (Rep.trivial k G ((Fin n → G) →₀ k))).ρ r _       refine x.induction_on ?_ (fun x y => ?_) fun y z hy hz => ?_       · rw [smul_zero, map_zero]       · rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, ← ofMulAction_self_smul_eq_mul]         exact (smul_tprod_one_asModule (Representation.ofMulAction k G G) r x y).symm       · rw [smul_add, hz, hy, map_add] }

group_cohomology.resolution.of_mul_actio.comment:
The `k[G]`-linear isomorphism `k[G] ⊗ₖ k[Gⁿ] ≃ k[Gⁿ⁺¹]`, where the `k[G]`-module structure on
the lefthand side is `TensorProduct.leftModule`, whilst that of the righthand side comes from
`Representation.asModule`. Allows us to use `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` to get a `k[G]`-basis

  AlternatingFaceMapComplex.obj (SimplicialObject.Augmented.drop.obj (compForgetAugmented.toModule k G)) ≅
    forget₂ToModuleCat k G
groupCohomology.resolution.compForgetAug.comment:
If we apply the free functor `Type u ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k` to the universal cover of the
classifying space of `G` as a simplicial set, then take the alternating face map complex, the result
is isomorphic to the standard resolution of the trivial `G`-representation `k` as a complex of
`k`-modules.

groupCohomology.dOne_comp_eq.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) :
  dOne A ∘ₗ ↑(oneCochainsLequiv A) = ↑(twoCochainsLequiv A) ∘ₗ (inhomogeneousCochains A).d 1 2
groupCohomology.dOne_comp_eq.comment:
Let `C(G, A)` denote the complex of inhomogeneous cochains of `A : Rep k G`. This lemma
says `dOne` gives a simpler expression for the 1st differential: that is, the following
square commutes:
```
  C¹(G, A) ---d¹-----> C²(G, A)
    |                      |
    |                      |
    |                      |
    v                      v
  Fun(G, A) -dOne-> Fun(G × G, A)
```
where the vertical arrows are `oneCochainsLequiv` and `twoCochainsLequiv` respectively.

groupCohomology.oneCoboundariesOfEq.comment:

groupCohomology.IsOneCocycle.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [Mul G] [AddCommGroup A] [SMul G A] (f : G → A) :
  Prop
groupCohomology.IsOneCocycle.comment:
A function `f : G → A` satisfies the 1-cocycle condition if
`f(gh) = g • f(h) + f(g)` for all `g, h : G`.

groupCohomology.IsOneCocycle.fullDefinition: def IsOneCocycle (f : G → A) : Prop := ∀ g h : G, f (g * h) = g • f h + f g

groupCohomology.IsTwoCocycle.comment:
A function `f : G × G → A` satisfies the 2-cocycle condition if

groupCohomology.IsTwoCocycle.fullDefinition: def IsTwoCocycle (f : G × G → A) : Prop :=   ∀ g h j : G, f (g * h, j) + f (g, h) = g • (f (h, j)) + f (g, h * j)

groupCohomology.IsMulOneCocycle.fullDefinition: def IsMulOneCocycle (f : G → M) : Prop := ∀ g h : G, f (g * h) = g • f h * f g
groupCohomology.IsMulOneCocycle.description: This definition states that a function from a group to a commutative group satisfies the multiplicative 1-cocycle condition if it fulfills a specific relationship involving the group operation and the structure of the commutative group.

groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCocycle.code:
groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCocycle.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Mul G] [CommGroup M] [SMul G M]
  (f : G × G → M) : Prop
groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCocycle.comment:
A function `f : G × G → M` satisfies the multiplicative 2-cocycle condition if
`f(gh, j) * f(g, h) = g • f(h, j) * f(g, hj)` for all `g, h : G`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f: This definition specifies the first morphism in a short complex within a category that accommodates zero morphisms.

groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCocycle.fullDefinition: def IsMulTwoCocycle (f : G × G → M) : Prop :=   ∀ g h j : G, f (g * h, j) * f (g, h) = g • (f (h, j)) * f (g, h * j)
groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCocycle.description: This definition specifies the conditions under which a function from a group to an abelian group qualifies as a multiplicative 2-cocycle by relating its values to the group's operations and scalar multiplications in a specified manner.

groupCohomology.map_one_of_isMulOneCocyc.code:
groupCohomology.map_one_of_isMulOneCocycle.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Monoid G] [CommGroup M]
  [MulAction G M] {f : G → M} (hf : IsMulOneCocycle f) : f 1 = 1

explanatories.groupCohomology.IsMulOneCocycle: This definition states that a function from a group to a commutative group satisfies the multiplicative 1-cocycle condition if it fulfills a specific relationship involving the group operation and the structure of the commutative group.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f: This definition specifies the first morphism in a short complex within a category that accommodates zero morphisms.

groupCohomology.map_one_of_isMulOneCocyc.description: This theorem asserts that if a function is a multiplicative 1-cocycle under the specified conditions, then its value at the identity element of the monoid is equal to the identity element of the group.

groupCohomology.map_one_fst_of_isMulTwoC.code:
groupCohomology.map_one_fst_of_isMulTwoCocycle.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Monoid G] [CommGroup M]
  [MulAction G M] {f : G × G → M} (hf : IsMulTwoCocycle f) (g : G) : f (1, g) = f (1, 1)

explanatories.groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCocycle: This definition specifies the conditions under which a function from a group to an abelian group qualifies as a multiplicative 2-cocycle by relating its values to the group's operations and scalar multiplications in a specified manner.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f: This definition specifies the first morphism in a short complex within a category that accommodates zero morphisms.

groupCohomology.map_one_fst_of_isMulTwoC.description: This theorem asserts that for a function defined on pairs of elements from a monoid that satisfies a specific cocycle condition, the value of that function at one element and any other element is the same as its value at the identity element paired with itself.

groupCohomology.IsMulOneCoboundary.code: groupCohomology.IsMulOneCoboundary.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommGroup M] [SMul G M] (f : G → M) : Prop
groupCohomology.IsMulOneCoboundary.comment:
A function `f : G → M` satisfies the multiplicative 1-coboundary condition if there's `x : M`
such that `g • x / x = f(g)` for all `g : G`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f: This definition specifies the first morphism in a short complex within a category that accommodates zero morphisms.

groupCohomology.IsMulOneCoboundary.fullDefinition: def IsMulOneCoboundary (f : G → M) : Prop := ∃ x : M, ∀ g : G, g • x / x = f g
groupCohomology.IsMulOneCoboundary.description: This definition characterizes a function from a group to a multiplicative group as satisfying the condition of being a 1-coboundary if there exists a specific element in the group such that the function can be expressed in terms of the action of the group on that element.

groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCoboundary.code:
groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCoboundary.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Mul G] [CommGroup M] [SMul G M]
  (f : G × G → M) : Prop
groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCoboundary.comment:
A function `f : G × G → M` satisfies the 2-coboundary condition if there's `x : G → M` such
that `g • x(h) / x(gh) * x(g) = f(g, h)` for all `g, h : G`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f: This definition specifies the first morphism in a short complex within a category that accommodates zero morphisms.

groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCoboundary.fullDefinition: def IsMulTwoCoboundary (f : G × G → M) : Prop :=   ∃ x : G → M, ∀ g h : G, g • x h / x (g * h) * x g = f (g, h)
groupCohomology.IsMulTwoCoboundary.description: A function from a group to a commutative group satisfies the 2-coboundary condition if it can be expressed in terms of another function that relates group actions via a specific multiplicative relationship involving the original function's values.

groupCohomology.H1.code: groupCohomology.H1.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) : Type u
groupCohomology.H1.comment:
We define the 1st group cohomology of a `k`-linear `G`-representation `A`, `H¹(G, A)`, to be
1-cocycles (i.e. `Z¹(G, A) := Ker(d¹ : Fun(G, A) → Fun(G², A)`) modulo 1-coboundaries
(i.e. `B¹(G, A) := Im(d⁰: A → Fun(G, A))`).

explanatories.groupCohomology.oneCocycles: This definition describes the 1-cocycles associated with a given representation of a group, characterizing them as the set of functions from the group to the module that remain invariant under the specific linear transformation induced by the group's multiplication.
explanatories.groupCohomology.oneCoboundaries: This definition describes the 1-coboundaries of a representation as the submodule comprising all elements obtained by taking the difference between the action of group elements on vectors and the vectors themselves.

groupCohomology.H1.fullDefinition: abbrev H1 := oneCocycles A ⧸ oneCoboundaries A
groupCohomology.H1.description: This definition establishes the first group cohomology for a given linear representation of a group over a commutative ring as the quotient of 1-cocycles by 1-coboundaries.

groupCohomology.H2.code: groupCohomology.H2.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) : Type u
groupCohomology.H2.comment:
We define the 2nd group cohomology of a `k`-linear `G`-representation `A`, `H²(G, A)`, to be
2-cocycles (i.e. `Z²(G, A) := Ker(d² : Fun(G², A) → Fun(G³, A)`) modulo 2-coboundaries
(i.e. `B²(G, A) := Im(d¹: Fun(G, A) → Fun(G², A))`).

explanatories.groupCohomology.twoCocycles: This definition describes the 2-cocycles associated with a given representation of a group, characterizing them as the set of functions from pairs of group elements to the module that remain invariant under a specific linear transformation induced by group multiplication.
explanatories.groupCohomology.twoCoboundaries: This definition specifies the 2-coboundaries in the context of group cohomology as the image of a map that transforms functions from the group to a representation space into functions from the product of the group with itself to the representation space, governed by a specific linear relation.

groupCohomology.H2.fullDefinition: abbrev H2 := twoCocycles A ⧸ twoCoboundaries A
groupCohomology.H2.description: This definition establishes the second group cohomology of a linear representation as the quotient of 2-cocycles by 2-coboundaries, providing a crucial algebraic structure for studying the representation's properties through cohomological methods.

groupCohomology.H0.code: groupCohomology.H0.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) : Submodule k (CoeSort.coe A)
groupCohomology.H0.comment:
We define the 0th group cohomology of a `k`-linear `G`-representation `A`, `H⁰(G, A)`, to be
the invariants of the representation, `Aᴳ`.

explanatories.Representation.invariants: This definition identifies the subspace of vectors that remain unchanged by all elements of a given group acting on a vector space.

groupCohomology.H0.description: This definition identifies the 0th group cohomology of a linear representation as the submodule consisting of elements that remain invariant under the action of the group.

groupCohomology.H0LequivOfIsTrivial.code:
groupCohomology.H0LequivOfIsTrivial.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) [A.IsTrivial] :
  ↥(H0 A) ≃ₗ[k] CoeSort.coe A
groupCohomology.H0LequivOfIsTrivial.comment: When the representation on `A` is trivial, then `H⁰(G, A)` is all of `A.`

explanatories.Rep.IsTrivial: This definition specifies a property for representations where every element acts trivially, effectively asserting that the representation does not change any elements.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofTop: This definition indicates that the entire module is linearly equivalent to the top submodule within it.

groupCohomology.H0LequivOfIsTrivial.fullDefinition: def H0LequivOfIsTrivial [A.IsTrivial] :     H0 A ≃ₗ[k] A := LinearEquiv.ofTop _ (invariants_eq_top A.ρ)
groupCohomology.H0LequivOfIsTrivial.description: This definition states that when a representation is trivial, the zeroth cohomology group associated with that representation is isomorphic to the underlying module of the representation itself.

groupCohomology.oneCoboundaries_eq_bot_o.code:
groupCohomology.oneCoboundaries_eq_bot_of_isTrivial.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G)
  [A.IsTrivial] : oneCoboundaries A = ⊥

groupCohomology.oneCoboundaries_eq_bot_o.description: This theorem demonstrates that in the context of a trivial representation, the set of one-coboundaries is empty, indicating that all functions in this space vanish.

groupCohomology.oneCocyclesLequivOfIsTri.code:
groupCohomology.oneCocyclesLequivOfIsTrivial.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G)
  [hA : A.IsTrivial] : ↥(oneCocycles A) ≃ₗ[k] Additive G →+ CoeSort.coe A
groupCohomology.oneCocyclesLequivOfIsTri.comment:
When `A : Rep k G` is a trivial representation of `G`, `Z¹(G, A)` is isomorphic to the
group homs `G → A`.

groupCohomology.oneCocyclesLequivOfIsTri.fullDefinition: @[simps] def oneCocyclesLequivOfIsTrivial [hA : A.IsTrivial] :     oneCocycles A ≃ₗ[k] Additive G →+ A where   toFun f :=     { toFun := f.1 ∘ Additive.toMul       map_zero' := oneCocycles_map_one f       map_add' := oneCocycles_map_mul_of_isTrivial f }   map_add' x y := rfl   map_smul' r x := rfl   invFun f :=     { val := f       property := mem_oneCocycles_of_addMonoidHom f }   left_inv f := by ext; rfl   right_inv f := by ext; rfl

groupCohomology.H1LequivOfIsTrivial.fullDefinition: def H1LequivOfIsTrivial [A.IsTrivial] :     H1 A ≃ₗ[k] Additive G →+ A :=   (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot _ (oneCoboundaries_eq_bot_of_isTrivial A)).trans     (oneCocyclesLequivOfIsTrivial A)

groupCohomology.H1_π.comment: The quotient map `Z¹(G, A) → H¹(G, A).`

groupCohomology.H1_π.fullDefinition: def H1_π : oneCocycles A →ₗ[k] H1 A := (oneCoboundaries A).mkQ

groupCohomology.shortComplexH0.fullDefinition: def shortComplexH0 : ShortComplex (ModuleCat k) :=   ShortComplex.moduleCatMk _ _ (dZero_comp_H0_subtype A)
groupCohomology.shortComplexH0.description: This definition describes a specific short complex associated with a representation of a group over a commutative ring, which consists of a sequence of modules capturing the invariants of the representation and the functions from the group to the module.

groupCohomology.dZero_comp_eq.code:
groupCohomology.dZero_comp_eq.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] (A : Rep k G) :
  dZero A ∘ₗ ↑(zeroCochainsLequiv A) = ↑(oneCochainsLequiv A) ∘ₗ (inhomogeneousCochains A).d 0 1
groupCohomology.dZero_comp_eq.comment:
Let `C(G, A)` denote the complex of inhomogeneous cochains of `A : Rep k G`. This lemma
says `dZero` gives a simpler expression for the 0th differential: that is, the following
square commutes:
```
  C⁰(G, A) ---d⁰---> C¹(G, A)
  |                    |
  |                    |
  |                    |
  v                    v
  A ---- dZero ---> Fun(G, A)
```
where the vertical arrows are `zeroCochainsLequiv` and `oneCochainsLequiv` respectively.

explanatories.HomologicalComplex.d: This defines the morphism between two components of a homological complex based on their indices and the structure of the complex.

groupCohomology.dZero_comp_eq.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of the zero differential with a specified equivalence of cochains yields a simpler expression for the transition between the zeroth and first levels of the cochain complex, confirming that the corresponding vertical maps commute in the diagram.

groupCohomology.dZeroArrowIso.fullDefinition: def dZeroArrowIso : Arrow.mk ((inhomogeneousCochains A).d 0 1) ≅     Arrow.mk (ModuleCat.ofHom (dZero A)) :=   Arrow.isoMk (zeroCochainsLequiv A).toModuleIso     (oneCochainsLequiv A).toModuleIso (dZero_comp_eq A)

groupCohomology.isMulOneCoboundary_of_is.code:
groupCohomology.isMulOneCoboundary_of_isMulOneCocycle_of_aut_to_units.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] (f : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) → Lˣ) (hf : IsMulOneCocycle f) : IsMulOneCoboundary f
groupCohomology.isMulOneCoboundary_of_is.comment:
Noether's generalization of Hilbert's Theorem 90: given a finite extension of fields and a
function `f : Aut_K(L) → Lˣ` satisfying `f(gh) = g(f(h)) * f(g)` for all `g, h : Aut_K(L)`, there
exists `β : Lˣ` such that `g(β)/β = f(g)` for all `g : Aut_K(L).`

fdRep.character.fullDefinition: def character (V : FDRep k G) (g : G) :=   LinearMap.trace k V (V.ρ g)
fdRep.character.description: The character of a representation associates each group element to the trace of the corresponding linear map associated with that representation.

FDRep.char_orthonormal.code:
FDRep.char_orthonormal.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] {G : Grp} [IsAlgClosed k] [Fintype ↑G] [Invertible ↑(Fintype.card ↑G)]
  (V W : FDRep k ↑G) [Simple V] [Simple W] :
  ⅟↑(Fintype.card ↑G) • ∑ g : ↑G, V.character g * W.character g⁻¹ = if Nonempty (V ≅ W) then 1 else 0
FDRep.char_orthonormal.comment:
Orthogonality of characters for irreducible representations of finite group over an
algebraically closed field whose characteristic doesn't divide the order of the group.
